text:
jin: Heads up — saw exporter CPU climb ~2.8x at 12:03 while ingesting a burst of small KV spans. p99 tail also moved from 40ms -> 220ms.
alyssa: ugh. which exporter? otlp-grpc? or our internal s3-archiver?
mike: otlp-grpc on the sidecar path. metrics ping: 
```
exporter_cpu{env="prod",component="otlp-grpc"} 2.8
span_ingest_rate{env="prod",type="kv_span"} 12800
exporter_p99_ms{env="prod",component="otlp-grpc"} 220
```
jin: exact. looks correlated with kv-span rate + many tiny attrs (avg size 560 bytes).
tara: quick theory: batching window too small, causing many tiny batches and more kernel/syscall overhead + marshalling cost. also we recently enabled attribute enrichment which allocates a lot.
dmitri: agree. payload shaping + batching are the two obvious knobs. also noticed threadpool thrash in logs: 
```
threadpool: workers=4 active=4 queue=0 rejected=0 backlog_spike=12
```
alyssa: can we flip to adaptive batch window? we have that flag in the exporter but it's off for prod.
mike: flag is: `exporter.batch.adaptive=false` in the config. enabling it changes batching from fixed 10ms -> adaptive up to 80ms on high QPS. we can test in canary.
ops-bot: deploy-created: canary/otlp-exporter-adaptive-2067890400 started (4 pods) by @mike
jin: rolled to canary 4 pods at 12:06. short run: CPU dropped ~22%, p99 from 220 -> 85ms after ~3 minutes.
dmitri: nice. what's the throughput impact? any increase in latency tail for spikes?
mike: throughput unchanged. micro-bench shows median latency slightly up (+5ms) but p99 improved. tradeoff seems acceptable.
tara: allocation flame: enrichment path dominated allocations — we can optimize by reusing attr buffers and skip enrichment for spans < 150 bytes as a fast-path.
alyssa: we should consider retention policy too — storing all kv spans for 7 days is heavy. can we sample low-value spans at ingest and mark them for lower retention?
dmitri: sampling at ingest is tricky w/ downstream guarantees. propose marking with `x-sample: low` then archiver can drop earlier. requires minimal schema change but ok.
jin: also found a pathological case where prefix cache lookups for certain keys do a linear scan; that woke GC. pushing a fix to O(n)->O(1) map lookup in route matcher now.
mike: experimental config change summary (canary): 
```
exporter.batch.adaptive=true
exporter.batch.max_ms=80
exporter.enrichment.fast_path_threshold=150
routing.cache.map=true
```
ops-bot: monitor: alert if exporter_cpu > 1.6x baseline for 5m or exporter_p99_ms > 150ms for 3m
alyssa: runbook note: if p99 > 150ms, scale canary to 8 pods and rollback `adaptive=false` if no improvement after 10m.
dmitri: tested a synthetic replay of burst (12k/s kv spans) locally with changes: CPU 1.3x baseline, p99 92ms, memory stable. adding results to perf doc.
tara: great. small follow-ups: (1) add unit test for attr buffer reuse, (2) add a short prometheus dashboard tile for span-size distribution, (3) add retention label `sample_tier` to span proto.
mike: can we do a gradual rollout via console rollout UX? aiming 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 20m with automatic rollback on p99 regress.
jin: yes, console rollout policy exists. set `canary=25` and `p99_slo=150ms` with rollback window 10m. I'll create the rollout.
ops-bot: rollout-scheduled: exporter-adaptive-rollout by @jin -> steps: [25%,50%,100%] window=20m p99_rollback=150ms
alyssa: timeline and next steps pinned: 1) monitor canary dashboards for 30m, 2) if stable, update retention docs and open infra PR for sampler, 3) perf PR for map lookup in route matcher.
jin: thanks team. saving logs/graphs to the thread and perf doc link: https://redwood.internal/perf/2067890123
mike: nice job catching this early :rocket:
jin: thanks — will follow up with PRs. :thumbsup:
